customConcept.blurb: Chicken sandwiches, waffle fries and a double drive-thru wrapped round the building, closed every Sunday since 1946. You run it; Chick-fil-A owns everything else.

setting.name: Harmony Crossing, suburban Atlanta
setting.desc: A freestanding restaurant on a busy retail road in the northern suburbs of Atlanta, between a supercenter and a high school. Commuters at breakfast, office workers and contractors at lunch, families and ball teams after practice, and a line of cars that sometimes reaches the road.

desk.title: The line is reaching the road

log.text: You're the Operator of a freestanding Chick-fil-A with a double drive-thru outside Atlanta. You put up $10,000; Chick-fil-A owns the land, the building and the equipment, takes 15% of sales, and splits what's left of the profit with you 50/50.

world.notes: This is a Chick-fil-A franchise run by an Operator. From the franchise disclosure documents: the Operator pays a $10,000 fee, Chick-fil-A owns or leases the real estate and owns the equipment, and the Operator pays a base operating service fee of 15% of sales (equipment rental comes out of that), plus rent, technology fees and half of the restaurant's remaining profit; the advertising contribution is currently 0%. Freestanding (non-mall) Chick-fil-As averaged $9.16 million in sales in 2025, down 1.7% from 2024; the chain had about 3,300 US restaurants and $23.9 billion of system sales. It has been closed on Sundays since 1946, serves breakfast until 10:30am, pressure-cooks its chicken in peanut oil, and was #1 in the American Customer Satisfaction Index for restaurants for eleven straight years until Jersey Mike's passed it in 2026. Operators can't own other active businesses, build no equity and can't pass the restaurant on. The menu follows chick-fil-a.com as of September 2026, including the limited-time Chicken & Waffles sandwiches and S'mores Milkshake; prices are rough national averages from a menu-price tracker and vary by restaurant, and a few (the Spicy Chicken Sandwich, the limited-time items, the Chicken, Egg & Cheese Biscuit, the muffin, floats and sodas) are estimates; the rent, labour and profit figures, the restaurant's name and the staff names are estimates or invented.

policies.name: Team member scholarships

franchise.rules: Chick-fil-A owns or leases the land and building and owns the equipment; the Operator leases them, signs the agreement personally, works in the restaurant full-time and can't run another active business. The 15% base operating service fee covers the equipment rental; on top of it Chick-fil-A charges rent and technology fees and takes half of the restaurant's remaining profit every month. The Operator builds no equity: the restaurant can't be sold or left to heirs. It's closed every Sunday, with no exceptions for stadium crowds or the Super Bowl. Chick-fil-A sets the menu, recipes, suppliers and national marketing; the Operator hires, trains and runs everything inside the four walls.

profile.name: Chick-fil-A, Inc.
profile.kind: privately held, family-owned restaurant company based in Atlanta
profile.desc: The Cathy family's company: about 3,300 US restaurants and nearly $24 billion of system sales in 2025, with more than 80% of Operators running a single restaurant.
profile.personality: Values-driven, famously selective about Operators and patient with those who treat guests well. It watches guest satisfaction as closely as sales, and it expects the restaurant to feel the same in Georgia as in Oregon.

rep.name: Marcus Whitlow
rep.title: Business consultant
rep.style: Visits every few weeks, sits in the dining room with a coffee, and asks how your team is doing before he asks about sales.

events.text: A national limited-time item launched with Chick-fil-A's marketing behind it, and the drive-thru lines got longer.
A supplier shortage hit sauces nationwide, and restaurants limited guests to one per item for a few weeks.

desk.title: Your business consultant has a suggestion
desk.text: Marcus thinks a second face-to-face ordering team in the drive-thru, with tablets, would take pressure off the lunch rush.

United States.mealTimes: Lunch around noon to 1pm, dinner from about 6 to 8pm.
United States.customs: Guests expect fast, attentive service, free tap water and refills, and a check brought on request. Tipping 18-22% is expected at table service.
United States.labour: At-will employment in most states; overtime after 40 hours a week; minimum wages set by state and city.
